question.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the absolute value on the left side of the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\frac{2x+1}{4}|-\frac{3}{2} & \le 1 \\ |\frac{2x+1}{4}| & \le \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value. 

The inequality specifies every number $\frac{2x+1}{4}$ whose distance from zero is less than or equal to $\frac{5}{2}.$ This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
\text{ }-\frac{5}{2}\le \frac{2x+1}{4}\le \frac{5}{2}
$$

Now, we can solve the compound inequality using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{2}\le \frac{2x+1}{4} & \le \frac{5}{2} \\ -10\le 2x+1 & \le 10 \\ -11\le 2x & \le 9 \\ -\frac{11}{2}\le x & \le \frac{9}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
